content.comment_body: [product_name] manual states that analog input signals are converted into digital values ranging from 0 to 1000. What does this mean in practice? I have a pressure sensor with a 4-20 mA signal and a range of 0-400 mbar. How should I set up the scaling? Is it sufficient to just enter the minimum and maximum values (0 to 400)?

Hello, For [product_name], 4 mA corresponds to a value of 0, and 20 mA equals 1000. Given your setup, a reading of 1000 would represent 400 mbar. You need to configure the scaling for the input accordingly. You can refer to [url] for more details on scaling questions. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking clarification on how [product_name] processes analog input signals, specifically how sensor readings should be mapped to the internal scale of 0-1000. The main uncertainty is about correctly aligning the analog range (4-20 mA, 0-400 mbar) with the device’s digital scale, due to insufficient details in the manual about scaling methods.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects easy-to-follow scaling instructions that directly translate sensor outputs to meaningful engineering units, preferring an intuitive process or the ability to simply set minimum and maximum values.
